title: Goodman hears the broadcast; Blue Balls renamed One O'Clock Jump
summary: Smith writes Jack Washington's part, Benny Goodman hears the broadcast and sends John Hammond, and the tune is renamed on air in Little Rock.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There's too many men blowing, going on (?) for him, and he says, "Well, I can't find a note, Prof." I said, "Well, I'll write you a part out." So I just wrote him a part out. So it got to a point... We were broadcasting that night, 12:30, and Benny Goodman heard it. And he said ...(?). . . "That drummer that they called on 'One O'Clock Jump,' that's a good
drummer. I want to send a man down there." So he sent John Hammond down there to listen to the band.
But you never got any royalties at all.

But that wasn't the name of it. It wasn't 'One O'Clock Jump' then. The name then was "Blue Balls." Ha-ha! When got down to Little Rock, we were down there working, then the man wanted to broadcast that night from 12:30 til 1 o'clock. And we got down there, and we (?)had to rent the phone(?) out...

So the man said, "Well, this thing here that you call 'Blue Balls,' we can't say that." He said, "The kids are listening to this program. We can't say that over the air. We can't do it." So Basie looked at me and said, "I told you that." I said, "You ain't told me nothin'." He said, "Well, we got to find a name for it." Basie says, "What are we going to do? What are we going to name it, Prof? Ain't you go no ideas?" I said, "No, let me think." He says, "Man, it ain't that long before we got to hit." He said, "Let me see." So the station man, he's sitting there, looking and looking and looking up at the clock. He said, "We ain't got but five minutes before we hit. You got to do something." He said, "Well, let me see. Let me think." He got to scratching his head. He said, "Since we're going to
play til 1, why not just call it 'One O'Clock Jump?'" So he said, "That's all right." And we let it stay that way.
